item.title: Re: “Green Crabs” they’re always green
item.content:encoded:
Okay, so, for starters, there are a LOT of little things.

Show Line-by-Line
Hide Line-by-Line

The picture is too high and needs a better caption.

"within a 15x30 meter minimal security biological containment cell in the E wing of Site 81, the containment cell’s interior’s roof is to be lined with a computer screen of a proportionate size which goes through a slideshow that auto generates a green screen every 5 minutes."
—>

  • Rooms have three dimensions, not two.
  • minimum security
  • in Site-81. (no need for E wing, end the sentence there)
  • "cell's interior's roof" —> "cell's ceiling"
  • "of a proportionate size" —> covering the whole ceiling.

"are to be obtained by ordinary means" —> what does this mean? Just say that you lock up or dispose of everything it eats.

"The colony is to be regulated in terms of population." give specifics, the researchers use these files as a guide in-universe.

"Foundation staff are recommended to not bring any personal green items near SCP-XXXX." —> awkward wording, please make this more concise.

"Description:" —> should be bolded.

" is a colony of an anomalous species of Carcinus maenas" —> it's the species, not the colony, isn't it? Give the laymen's term for the species as well please.

"SCP-XXXX can survive on land or water indefinitely, weigh 141 to 453 grams and grow up to be 6 to 10 centimeters tall, and can survive in any natural environment." this sentence is all over the place. take one sentence to describe the average specimen, then another to describe it's habitat / survival needs.

"SCP-XXXX is capable of reproduction" it's a species, this is sort of a given.

" the instances produced during reproduction possess the same anomalous properties as SCP-XXXX, crossbreeds of SCP-XXXX have been found to lack SCP-XXXX’s anomalous properties," this sentence doesn't really add anything; it can and should be cut. Also, if you keep it, the sentence should end there, after "properties"

"SCP-XXXX instead survives by gaining sustenance from converting the color green into energy using a process similar to photosynthesis but modified to suit SCP-XXXX’s needs which also requires the extraction of green color from any object modifying said object to become a grey color, this effect does not affect SCP-XXXX instances nor art created by “Viridian Von Zakavich”, the effect has currently been found to be irreversible." —->

  • This is one sentence; it should be three.
  • the word "instead" is unnecessary.
  • simplify the first bit into "it eats the color green" but more clinical, such as "SCP-XXXX obtains sustenance by draining the color green from surrounding matter."
  • Does it only eat green? Or anything pigment with green in it, such as white? Specify in a footnote please.
  • "'Viridian Von Zakavich', the effect" this is a comma splice, which is bad. either make it a semicolon or separate them into two sentences. Also, it flows better if the "Viridian" part comes after the effect is fully explained.

"SCP-XXXX has been shown to keep doing said activity even when unnecessary, the duration of time that the process takes is dependent on the size of the object." —->

  • What activity? Eating? Specify.
  • "the duration" should be the start of a new sentence.
  • "dependent on" should be "proportional to".
  • "Size" should probably be "surface area" assuming it doesn't eating the color of the interior.
  • Again, the effect should be fully explained before changing topics.

"SCP-XXXX survives solely through this process, so it is incapable of producing waste matter."

  • Just say it doesn't eat by any other means.
  • The waste matter bit is unrelated and should be a different sentence.

"Every part of SCP-XXXX is incapable of appearing as any color other than the same shade of green such as when viewed, during the day, during the night, using a colored filter, with an x-ray, or by a color-blind person." —->
Simplify this to something like "SCP-XXXX will always appear green, regardless of light level, color filters, or visual impairments.

"This property also occurs when SCP-XXXX is referred to in text, or depicted in an artistic rendition." —-> no need for the comma after "text". Show me the green in text property or delete it entirely.

"When SCP-XXXX comes in contact with any type of material that would change its overall color, SCP-XXXX will adapt instantaneously to the material to have its color remain unaltered." —-> wordy and awkward, just say that it's always green and incapable of changing color.

"SCP-XXXX will also grow distressed and agitated if referred to as any color other than green in a speech that is audible to SCP-XXXX." —-> weird but okay

"Embedded Foundation agents were able to determine that a large colony of an invasive green crab population found in the storage of an art gallery in Greenwood City was connected to an artist by the name of “Viridian Von Zakavich”." —-> don't just throw us in hot here, tell us what made them get discovered in the first place. As it is, you're just telling us, "we figured out Viridian was behind it!" without properly explained what the inciting incident was.

"Mobile Task Force Epsilon-6 “village idiots” were " —-> "Village Idiots"

"mongoloids" DO NOT USE THIS WORD, call them primitive or something. Jesus.

There are other little things within the interview, but I won't go over them for now, because it needs a rehaul. You're character comes off as a bit too two-dimensional. I can see the character you're trying to create (full of himself, snobby, etc.), but he's coming off way to strong here. His first text block has him going from being honored to saying he doesn't have all day. Be more subtle and consistent with his dialogue.
